title: Revealed: inside the US military's plan to tap huge sums from the NIH
abstract: An agreement paves the way for hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of projects to be transferred from the NIH’s institute for infectious diseases to the Department of Defense.

title: Optical excitation of nonreciprocal antiferromagnetic magnons at sub-terahertz frequencies
authors: Chang Xu, Hanbum Park, Shishun Zhao, et al.
abstract: The authors demonstrate that optically excited subterahertz magnons in canted antiferromagnetic hematite propagate nonreciprocally at high group velocities, offering potential for ultrafast spintronic applications.

title: Unconditional and exponentially large violation of classicality
authors: Marcello Benedetti, Gabriel Marin-Sanchez, Jordi Weggemans, et al.
abstract: The authors introduce a practical game that distinguishes quantum from classical behaviour without relying on unproven assumptions. Quantum computers achieve exponentially larger scores than any classical strategy, a result confirmed in experiments.

title: Steric control of signaling bias in the immunometabolic receptor GPR84
authors: Pinqi Wang, Xuan Zhang, Abdul-Akim Guseinov, et al.
abstract: This study reveals how subtle changes in ligand structure control signaling bias at the immunometabolic receptor GPR84, providing structural details for the rational design of drugs with tailored signalling properties.

title: OXR1 is a dual redox–mitochondrial checkpoint governing osteoclast differentiation and bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model
authors: Xiaojun Chen, Chengyu Zhou, Xiangyun Jin, et al.
abstract: Osteoclasts need to manage reactive oxygen species by coordinating redox control and mitochondrial quality maintenance. Here, the authors identify OXR1 as a regulator of osteoclastogenesis and mitophagy, and show that genetic or pharmacological targeting of OXR1 attenuates bone loss in an osteoporosis mouse model.

title: Selectively intraparticle oxygen dissociation and metalloid mineralization for long-term groundwater remediation
authors: Chaohuang Chen, Zhongyuan Guo, Qianhai Zhou, et al.
abstract: Toxic arsenic, antimony and selenium in groundwater are mineralized inside lattice-modified iron nanoparticles with a 98-fold greater stability during long-term aging in groundwater, offering an economic in-situ remediation strategy.

title: Whole genome sequencing of 1427 Mexican individuals from the oriGen cohort
authors: Israel Aguilar-Ordoñez, Eugenio Guzman-Cerezo, David Torres-Treviño, et al.
abstract: Mexican populations remain underrepresented in genomics. Here, Aguilar-Ordoñez et al. report on 1,481 whole-genomes from the oriGen project, identifying key variants like a CNV driving the Rh-negative blood group.

title: Thermal conductivity predictions with foundation atomistic models
authors: Balázs Póta, Paramvir Ahlawat, Gábor Csányi, et al.
abstract: Researchers show how foundation atomistic models can predict heat transport and thermal expansion, using physics-based benchmarks and fine-tuning to reach first-principles accuracy.

title: Neoadjuvant PD1 plus CTLA-4 immune checkpoint blockade in surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma: a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial
authors: Lu Sun, Lauren F. Markus, Julio C. Sanchez, et al.
abstract: Here the authors report clinical and immunological outcomes of a randomized surgical window-of-opportunity trial designed to test whether dual immune checkpoint blockade targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4 could overcome the adaptive immune resistance previously reported with single-agent anti-PD-1 therapy in patients with surgically resectable recurrent glioblastoma.
